I have been working this land for 55 years. My father farmed before me. I know this soil, I know when it is thirsty, I know when the wheat is struggling. I do not read books. I read the crops.

My land is 3 mu. Same land, wheat in winter, maize in summer. This is how we have always done it here in Quzhou. My wife and I can manage 3 mu still. Just the two of us now.

**Wheat** goes in October after the maize comes off. I will use the improved variety seed I buy from the village supply store — the same kind I used last two years, it did well. Before sowing I will run the rotary tiller through once to break up the stubble. I put down compound fertilizer as base, then top-dress with urea around Chinese New Year when the wheat starts to green up again. Irrigation three times: once before sowing to get good germination, once at jointing, once at heading when the grain is filling. In spring I spray once for weeds and once for rust and aphids — that field gets rust bad some years. I expect maybe 450 jin per mu, around 450 kg. Has been that way for years.

**Maize** goes in right after wheat harvest in June, no time to waste. I buy hybrid seed — the hybrid gives more grain, everyone here uses hybrid for maize. I rotary till lightly, sow, then fertilize twice: base compound fertilizer at planting, urea top-dress at the big bell stage. Irrigate two or three times depending on rain — the summer rains usually help. One spray for fall armyworm, they have been bad the last few years. I expect 550 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

I will not change much this year. At 75 I am not experimenting. What works, works.
